_doc: #1841 one corpus for the Rust core (src/tests.rs) and its Kotlin twin (BrowserCoreListsTest): each case runs `op` on `in`; every key of `out` must equal the answer's key (deep, object key order ignored).

cases.name: history_load sorts newest first, defaults the title to the url, drops blank rows
history_load on text that is not a list is empty
history_load on a json object is empty
history_load keeps an empty title and reads a numeric string ts
history_record moves a revisited url to the top (no duplicate row), blank title becomes the url
history_record ignores about:blank and a blank url
history_dedupe keeps the newest row per url
history_query filters by title or url, trimmed and case-blind, input order kept
history_query sort host (www, port, path ignored; newer first on a tie)
history_query sort frecency (recency bands, newer first within a band)
history_query ranked: host prefix, then title prefix, then substring
history_import merges: newer wins, new rows added, junk skipped
history_import reads a bare array text
visitlog_merge folds history into the log, no repeated (url, time), newest first, capped
visitlog_merge reads the stored u/t/s text
bm_load keeps the order, defaults the title, drops blank urls
bm_add updates the url in place at the top and normalises the folder
bm_folders lists every folder with its parents, sorted
bm_move_folder moves the subtree, not a sibling with the same prefix
bm_move_folder from the top level is a no-op
bm_delete_folder of the top level removes nothing
bm_edit changes title and folder, keeps the time
bm_edit of an unknown url changes nothing
bm_sections: top level first, then folders sorted
bm_view narrows by chip, then every word of the query
bm_view with no chip and a blank query is every section
bm_merge_seed applies each entry once, moves a legacy group, never re-adds a seen one
bm_merge_seed with everything seen and the version stored is not a write
bm_merge_seed with no items does nothing
bm_import: newer replaces, new rows appended with a normalised folder, blank skipped
migrate history: the old reader's quirks become the canonical list
migrate history already canonical is not a rewrite
migrate history that is not a list is invalid (kept untouched by the caller)
migrate bookmarks keeps the order and every field
weby_load of nothing is the seed (null)
weby_all: browser bookmarks by folder, Quickmarks, then the catalogue
weby_all with nothing but the catalogue
dl_index_load keeps rows with an id, reads a numeric string id, defaults the rest
dl_index_add puts the new row first, replaces its id, caps
dl_jobs_load keeps every field, drops a row without an id, an unknown state is paused, a process death re-queues RUNNING
dl_policy of nothing is the defaults
dl_jobs_query by state name, any case
dl_jobs_query by file name, any case
migrate download jobs keeps a RUNNING row as it is
